items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But when Vanessa Williams came, that year, there was – you could almost sense it. There’s something about her.

ctx.x: What was that like, to play for the . . . ?

That was nice. It was a challenge. It used to be awfully hard in the beginning, because we used to go on Tuesday. On Tuesday evening we’d start rehearsing. We’d rehearse all night and get up early the next morning and rehearse, and do the first

performance, the elimination performance, on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Then Saturday they did the show live on the air. It was a lot of work. Then after that – because at that time, they didn’t do any pre-recording. You really – you just ground until you were playing on your teeth, almost. There was so much music. Then, as the years went by, they began doing a lot of pre-recording, because they had a lot of things like production numbers, where it was impossible for these people to be running around with…
